about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Old-crop has bounced with Dec back to ~76 (+1.4%) and Mar near 80 despite a firm dollar, a technical recovery rather than new supply news. Dec deliveries and the high-grade share of certificated stock still cap the comfort for longs until Mar is the lead month.
events: Strong dollar weighed on cotton early (ADMIS)
Dec ~76.0, Mar ~79.8 by midday (ICE via TradingView)
Texas yield trimmed again in USDA's November report (RFD-TV)

sugar.fundamental: The Brazil-led slide held into the afternoon: the real weakened further to ~5.93 per dollar (about -2.7% on the day) and Mar raws traded ~17.15, near session lows. A cheaper real lifts mills' local-currency return on exports, so Centre-South export hedging is likely to keep pressing rallies while the currency is unstable.
events: Mar raws ~17.15 (-4.9%) on the weak real (Barchart, ICE via Yahoo)
USD/BRL ~5.93 as LatAm currencies sell off with equities (Yahoo, Reuters)
India seeks fresh raw-sugar import offers (Reuters)

coffee.fundamental: Arabica shrugged off the weaker real, with Dec up to ~282 as lower Colombian shipments trimmed washed-arabica availability. Falling ICE certified stocks keep Dec deliverability the key support; Brazil producer selling into a weak real is the main risk to the Dec/Mar inverse.
events: Colombian coffee exports fall, lifting arabica (Barchart)
ICE certified arabica stocks keep declining (ICE)

cocoa.fundamental: The rebound extended with Dec ~5,030 (+3.8%), still a short-covering move off the ~4,980 support. Nothing new on supply: ICE stocks are rising and the West African main crop looks better, so the bounce runs against the fundamentals.
events: Cocoa Dec up ~3.8% to ~5,030 (ICE via Yahoo)
Rising ICE inventories still weigh on the balance (Barchart)
Ghana plans to phase out raw bean exports by 2030 (Reuters)
